Original Law.Subject: Suspension of Issuance of Letters of Authority (L/As) and All Ongoing Audits/Investigations; and Submission of Inventory of L/As
Original Law.To: All Regional Directors, Revenue District Officers and Others Concerned

Details.Details:
Purpose

The purpose of this Revenue Memorandum Order is to establish a baseline for rationalizing the audit workload of audit and investigating divisions, revenue district offices and other units as a foundation for updating existing examination policies and reorienting audit programs of the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR).

It is therefore necessary to determine the current status of all tax cases which are still pending action in the National Office and Regional Offices by suspending issuance of letters of authority to audit or investigate, as well as ongoing audit and investigation of tax cases for all years and requiring an inventory of all L/As.

Suspension of issuance of letters of authority

Due to the impending reorganization of the BIR, issuance of letters of authority to audit/investigate, as well as on-going audit/investigation of internal revenue taxes for all years are hereby suspended. This suspension shall not apply to the following cases:

1. The investigation of tax cases which will prescribe this year under the statute of limitations; casia

2. Estate and donor's tax cases;

3. Cases involving the transfer of shares of stocks and real property, requiring certificate authorizing registration;

4. Claims for VAT credit/refund (input tax) under the One-Stop-Shop;

5. Those specifically to be authorized by the undersigned.

Accountable Forms Division

The Chief, Accountable Forms Division, shall submit (in a form prescribed in Annex "A") a report on the quantity of L/As (BIR Form No. 19.65) which were requisitioned and issued to the various audit and investigating units for the period from January 1, 1991 to May 31, 1993.

Accountable Forms Officer

The Regional Director, Chief, Intelligence and Investigation Office, Assistant Commissioner (or Officer-in-Charge). Special Operations Service and Excise Tax Service, and heads of special audit investigating groups or teams, accountable for the preparation and approval of L/As, shall submit a report of accountability of L/As received for the period January 1, 1991 to May 31, 1993 using the form prescribed in Annex "B".

Heads of audit/investigating units

The Revenue District Officer and other heads of audit investigating units (e.g., audit divisions, special audit teams and/or groups and the Intelligence and Investigation Office) shall submit a report (in a form prescribed in Annex "C") on the status of L/As issued/served. For purposes of accomplishing Annex "C", L/As issued/served refer to those which were previously received by the accountable forms officer during the period from January 1, 1991 to May 31, 1993 and subsequently referred to the audit investigating units. casia

Deadline for submission

The above reports should be submitted to the Assessment Service not later than June 30, 1993.

(Sgd.) LIWAYWAY VINZONS-CHATO
Commissioner

Original Law.Subject: Employees Suggestions and Incentive Awards System
Original Law.To: All Revenue Officials and Employees

Details.Details:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Rule X of the Omnibus rules Implementing Book V of Executive Order No. 292, the Employee Suggestions and Incentive Award System of the Bureau of Internal Revenue is hereby established. acd

I. Objective

A. General:

To recognize and reward officials and employees of the Bureau, individually or in groups, for their suggestions, inventions, superior accomplishments, and other personal efforts which contribute to the efficiency, economy, or other improvement in the operation of the BIR, or for other extraordinary acts or services in the public interest and for exemplary service and conduct.

B. Specific:

1. To encourage creativity, innovativeness for an efficient, responsive and progressive public service;

2. To foster among the officials and employees in the BIR the awareness and desire to maintain or sustain exemplary performance and superior accomplishments; and acd

3. To motivate the officials and employees of the BIR to contribute to national development through increased productivity.

II. Scope

The Systems shall apply to all officials and employees in the first and second levels of the career or non-career service of the BIR, whether or not they receive compensation, regardless of amount.

III. Types of Contributions

Under the System, any of the following types of contribution shall be entitled to an award:

A. Idea type contribution - this shall refer to an idea, a suggestion, an invention for improvement to effect economy in operation, to increase production, improve working condition or service,

B. Performance type contribution - this shall refer to:

1. Performance of an extraordinary act or service in the public interest in connection with, or related to, one's official employment; or

2. Outstanding community service or heroic acts in the public interest; or

3. Sustained work performance for a minimum period of one year which is over and above the normal position requirement of the individual or group; or aisa dc

4. Exemplary service and conduct.

IV. Types of Awards

A. Honor Award shall consist of:

1. The Agency or the "Kapwa" Award which shall be given to an individual or group of individuals in recognition of contributions from an idea or performance resulting in direct benefits to a single agency. Nominations for this category need not be submitted to the Civil Service Commission for screening and evaluation. The SIAC shall evaluate the nominations for this category and recommend to the head of the BIR the most qualified nominees. 

This award shall consist of a gold (gilded) medallion and a plaque containing the citation and signature of the head of BIR.

B. The incentive awards may consist of the following:

1. Performance Incentive shall be given to an employee who has obtained an Outstanding or Very Satisfactory rating based on the BIR Approved Performance Evaluation System for the last two successive evaluation periods. The incentive award shall be in the form of step increments in accordance with the provisions of the joint CSC-DBM Circular No. 1, s. 1990. Provided, That the total number of recipients of step increments based on merit in any one (1) calendar year shall not be more than ten (10%) per cent of the total number of personnel actually employed in the agency, provided that the total number of recipients of two step increments shall not exceed three per cent (3%) thereof.

2. Length of Service Incentive shall be given to an employee who has rendered at least three years of continuous satisfactory service in a particular position and which shall consist of step increments in accordance with the provisions of Joint CSC-DBM Circular No. 1, s. 1990. casia

3. Productivity Incentive shall be given to an employee or group of employees who has exceeded their targets or has incurred incremental improvement over existing targets subject to prevailing policies on the matter.

4. Most Courteous Employee Award shall be given to an employee in accordance with the criteria and standards established under CSC MC No. 15, s. 1990 which instituted the Courtesy Campaign Program in the Civil Service, known as the "Ang Magalang, Bow".

5. Loyalty Award shall be granted to an employee who has completed at least ten (10) years of continuous and satisfactory service in the particular agency granting the award. The grant of this loyalty award shall be in accordance with CSC Memorandum Circular No. 42, s. 1992. acd

6. Retirement Award shall be given to a retiree who had rendered at least fifteen (15) years of satisfactory government service. This award shall be in the form of a plaque of appreciation, the design and citation of which shall be determined by the office concerned.

7. Cost Economy Measure Award shall be granted to an employee whose contribution in terms of suggestions or inventions or performance of functions result in monetary savings, or results combined monetary saving and intangible benefits, the amount of cash award shall be determined in terms of a certain percentage of its estimated total value or benefit but not to exceed 20%.

8. Star Award shall be given to employee/s who are directly involve in the assessment and collection of internal revenue taxes. The following awards shall be given to winner (s) in each category.

a. Special Tax Achievement Recognition Award - a bronze medal with ribbon.

b. Superior Tax Achievement Recognition Award - a silver medal with ribbon.

c. Supreme Tax Achievement Recognition Award - a gold medal with ribbon. casia

Awardees shall be given priority in promotion provided she/he meets the qualification requirements for the position. Cash Prizes shall be given to the awardees subject to the availability of funds.

The respective group supervisor or RDO of the winning Revenue Officers shall be awarded citations in recognition of the assistance and guidance they extended to the winners in the exemplary performance of their work.

10. Such other incentive awards which the BIR SIAC may decide to give, subject to the approval of the head of the BIR and the CSC

V. Suggestion and Incentive Award Committee

A. Composition

A suggestion and Incentive Award Committee (SIAC) which shall be composed of the following is hereby created in the BIR to administer the Systems. It shall be composed of the following:

a. Two Deputy Commissioners

b. Asst. Commissioner (Administrative Service)

c. Chief, Personnel Division

d. Representative from the Legal Service, and

e. Two rank and file representatives to be elected at large thru an election. cd i

B. Selection Procedure

The BIR SIAC may adopt the following procedures in the selection of nominee/s to any of the incentive awards enumerated above:

1. Establish criteria/qualification of nominees

2. Review of documents;

2.1 Personnel Data Sheet; or

2.2 Service Record; or

2.3 Performance Appraisal Rating for the last two (2) rating periods; or

2.4 Courteous Service Form; or

2.5 Nomination form containing the act/idea/ suggestion/invention and the subsequent result or effect which may neither be monetary or non-monetary or which has direct benefit to the Agency; or

2.6 Any other documents to support the nomination. cda

3. Determine the form of incentive award to be granted; and

4. Prepare the necessary recommendation to the Head of Agency.

VI. Funding

The Bureau of Internal Revenue shall set aside in its annual budget the necessary appropriations to cover whatever expenses that may be incurred in granting both monetary and non-monetary awards in accordance with the provisions of this ESIAS. cd

VII. Effectivity

The Bureau of Internal Revenue ESIAS shall take effect upon approval by the Civil Service Commission, or its duly authorized representative.

Recommending Approval:

VICTOR DEOFERIO JR.
Deputy Commissioner
(Officer-in-Charge)

April 29, 1993

Approved:

PATRICIA A. STO. TOMAS
Chairman

Bureau of Internal Revenue
BIR Road, Quezon City

Dear Deputy Commissioner Deoferio:

We are returning to you The Employee Suggestions and Incentive Awards (ESIAS) and Performance Evaluation System (PES) of that Bureau, duly approved. casia

As regards the PES, it is necessary that the following requirements be met before the System is fully implemented:

1. The system shall be pilot-tested for at least one (1) rating period and the Commission shall be informed of the pilot-testing results when completed, and

2. If improvements are to be made after the pilot-testing and prior to actual implementation, the Commission shall be furnished the revised copy of the System.

Original Law.Subject: Submission of Briefing Paper for Past Performance
Original Law.To: All Revenue Regional Directors, All Revenue District Officers

Details.Details:
1. Background

The performance efficiency of every head of office in charge with the implementation of the revenue laws is determined by his ability to review what he has done and to develop plans to improve on his past performance. In order that the Regional Directors and the Revenue District Officers who are directly in charge with planning, managing, supervising, directing and coordinating the operations and activities for tax administration, they should develop their own implementation programs/projects within their areas of authority and responsibility and within the framework of existing policies and procedures. cd i

2. Contents of the Briefing Paper

Review of past performance should include, not only the accomplishments in terms of how much was collected but also what programs and projects were developed to implement the Tax Administration Program in 1992 and for the period from January 1 to May 31, 1993. The BP should describe, by way of short statements, such programs and what results were accomplished by each program.

3. Problem Identification.

Each Regional Director and Revenue District Officer should likewise state the problems which he has encountered in the course of the performance of his managerial and supervisory duties and how he resolved or intends to resolve such problems.

4. Action Plan for July 1 - December 31, 1993

An Action Plan should be developed and submitted stating how performance will be improved. The Plan should embody specific measures and proposals for improving the administration of the revenue laws and regulations at the regional level (for the Regional Director) and at the district level (for the Revenue District Officer), as well as methods of how, the proposed measures will be implemented.

The Regional Director should conduct strategic planning sessions with his staff and RDOs from June 1 to June 20, 1993. acd

5. Timetable.

To avoid delay, the Briefing Paper should be transmitted directly to the Chief Planning and Research Division not later than June 20, 1993, for evaluation and consolidation.

6. Performance Evaluation

The performance of each Regional Director and Revenue District Officer shall be evaluated on the basis of how efficiently and effectively he implements his Action Plans covering the period from July 1 - December 31, 1993 designed to meet his revenue goals.

(Sgd.) Liwayway Vinzons-Chato
Commissioner

Original Law.Subject: Guidelines and Procedures on the Printing, Requisitioning, Issuance and Distribution of BIR Tax Return Forms to Revenue Regional and District Offices
Original Law.To: All Internal Revenue Officers and Others Concerned

Details.Details:
I. OBJECTIVES:

This Order is issued to:

A. Improve the procedures in the printing, requisitioning, issuance and distribution of all BIR tax return forms:

B. Save on cost and avoid the printing, requisitioning and issuance of tax return forms inexcessive quantities; and

C. Reduce, if not totally eliminate, wastage and delay in the distribution of BIR tax return forms.

II. GUIDELINES:

In order to attain the above objectives, the following guidelines are hereby prescribed for the information and compliance of all concerned:

A. The Property Division (PD) shall determine the quantity of tax return forms for printing based on the actual number of taxfilers of the preceding year to be provided by the Computer and Information Systems Service (CISS) plus 100% allowance for annual, monthly and quarterly tax returns.

B. The Properly Division (PD) shall issue on or before December 15 of each year, a one-year supply of income tax return forms directly to the Revenue District Offices (RDOs) or thru the Administrative Branches (Adm. Br.) based on the agreement made during a meeting between the Administrative Branch chiefs and National Office officials on the proper distribution of the tax return forms (See Annex A - System of Distribution of Tax Return Forms Requirements for the Revenue Regions). Tax return forms for VAT, non-VAT, percentage and other taxes which are filed monthly or quarterly shall be issued to the RDOs one month before the start of each quarter.

C. The transit invoice and Requisition and Issue Voucher (RIV) accompanying every shipment shall be acknowledged and returned to the Property Division within ten (10) days from receipt thereof.

D. The volume of tax return forms to be distributed to the RDOs shall be based on the actual number of taxfilers of the preceding year plus an allowance of 50% to provide for new/additional taxfilers and other users.

E. The RDOs may request for additional tax return forms as the need arises, provided it is duly justified and duly approved by the Regional Director concerned or his Assistant.

F. The Property Division shall approve only those requisitions by the RDOs which are duly approved by the Regional Director or his Assistant, in addition to those requisitions from International Tax Affairs Division (ITAD) and Tax Information and Assistance Division (ITAD).

G. RDOs from far flung regions without regular means of transportation shall receive their supply thru the Administrative Branch which shall be responsible for the delivery of forms to its respective districts.

H. All Revenue District Officers and other BIR personnel concerned shall observe stricter control in the distribution of BIR tax return forms to taxpayers. If request exceeds ten (10) sets, the taxpayer shall be required to fill up a request form (see Annex B - Request for BIR Tax Return Forms).

I. Corollary to H, all requests for tax return forms shall be properly recorded. A record using the Allocation/Distribution of Tax Return Forms marked Annex C shall be maintained by the district for every BIR Form available for distribution.

J. The District Offices shall issue forms only to taxpayers falling within its jurisdiction. However, in the case of those requests for tax return forms in bulk for the employees of the company or agency, the RDO nearest it may issue the needed tax return forms provided they accomplish the prescribed request form.

K. The RDOs are required to add one (1) extra copy for the set which is presently composed of three (3) copies to allow for the taxpayer's draft when preparing his tax return. In this regard, no single taxpayer may be given an extra set for his same purpose.

III. PROCEDURES:

The following are the procedures on the printing, requisitioning, issuance and distribution of BIR tax return forms.

A. Revenue District Offices (RDOs)

1. Submit to Property Division the RIV for:

a) income tax returns based on the preceding year's, income taxfilers plus 50% allowance, not later than November 15 of each year.

b) all returns other than ITRs based on the number of taxfilers of the previous quarter plus 50% allowance, two months before the start of each quarter.

c) additional requisitions for income and other tax returns together with the corresponding justification as approved by the Regional Director concerned or his Assistant, whenever necessary.

2. Require the taxpayers to fill up and sign the "Request for BIR Tax Return Form" (See Annex B) indicating the quantity, if the request is for more than ten (10) sets.

3. Issue/distribute the tax return forms to taxpayers/other users based on the submitted "Request for BIR Tax Return Forms" or as requested for those not exceeding ten (10) sets.

4. Maintain a record of issued tax return forms using the Allocation/Distribution of Tax Return Form (Annex C) to keep track of the daily inventory/availability of each type of tax return form and which shall be subject to verification in the management audit.

5. Prepare the Monthly Summary of BIR Tax Return Forms Issued (see Annex E) in four (4) copies, to be submitted not later than the 15th day of the succeeding month to the following:

B. Computer and Information Systems Service (CISS)

Provide Property Division not later than May 31st of each year with a summary report of tax returns filed of the preceding year by RDO to be used as basis in determining the number of tax return forms to be issued to every RDO.

C. Property Division (PD)

1. Take note of the schedules of the different tax return forms as shown in Forms Calendar (Annex D) from the preparation of the request for printing to the distribution to RDOs and Administrative Branches.

2. Deliver on or before December 15 of each year, the one year supply of income tax return forms directly to RDOs or thru the Administrative Branch, as the case may be, based on the aforementioned summary report received from CISS upon receipt of the RIV;

3. Deliver one month before the start of each quarter the other tax return forms (VAT, non-VAT, percentage and other taxes) upon receipt of the RIV;

4. Approve/Disapprove request for additional requisition based on aforementioned guidelines.

5. Distribute/deliver the tax return forms in accordance with the system of distribution described in Annex A.

Direct to RDOs

a) Delivery direct to the RDOs shall be made for the Regions and RDOs located within Metro Manila namely: RRs 3B, 4B1, 4B2, 4A - only for RDOs 22, 23, 24 and 25 and 4C - only for RDOs 37, 37A, 38, 38A and 39 (See Annex A, Column 1).

b) Delivery via the forwarders direct to RDOs 26, 27, 42 and 43 of RR 4A (See Annex A, Column 2).

Thru the Administrative Branch

c) Delivery shall be direct to the Administrative Branches of RR 3A (for all RDOs) and RDOs 40 and 41 of RR 4C (See Annex A, Column 3).

d) Delivery via the forwarders to the Administrative Branches of RRs 1, 1A, 2, 5, 6A, 6B, 7, 8, 9, 10A, 10B, 11A and 11B (See Annex A, Column 4).

D. Administrative Branch (Adm. Br.)

1. Receive and distributive tax return forms upon delivery by the Property Division to all RDOs under RR 3A and RDOs 40 and 41 of RR 4C (See Annex A, column 3).

2. Receive tax return forms via Forwarders for RRs 1, 1A, 2, 5, 6A, 6B, 7, 8, 9, 10A, 10B, 11A and 11B and distribute them to the respective districts (See Annex A, column 4).

IV. TRANSITORY PROVISION:

All RDOs shall start issuing tax return forms in accordance with the new guidelines and procedures beginning July 1, 1993. It shall be clear that from this date the prescribed Annex C shall be accomplished and maintained and the required Annex E shall be submitted not later than the 15th day of August, 1993 for the initial report and on or before the 15th day of the succeeding months for the subsequent reports.

With regard to tax return forms for VAT, Non-VAT, percentage and other taxes for the third quarter, the required RIV must be prepared and submitted to Property Division not later than May 31, 1993.

V. REPEALING CLAUSE:

This Order amends and/or repeals existing orders and/or portions thereof inconsistent herewith.

VI. EFFECTIVITY:

This Order shall take effect immediately.

(Sgd.) LIWAYWAY VINZONS-CHATO
Commissioner of Internal Revenue

Original Law.Subject: Merit Promotion Plan
Original Law.To: All Revenue Officials and Employees

Details.Details:
Pursuant to the provisions of Section 32, Book V of Executive Order No. 292, otherwise known as the Administrative Code of 1987, Resolution No. 83-343, promulgating the revised rule on promotion, CSC Memorandum Circular No. 3, s. 1979 as amended by Memorandum Circular No. 18, s. 1988, and Memorandum Circular No. 38, s. 1989, this Merit Promotion Plan (MPP) is hereby established for the guidance of all concerned. cdt

I. OBJECTIVES

It is hereby declared the policy of the Bureau of Internal Revenue to adhere strictly to the merit principle in the promotion of employees. In the implementation of this policy, the following objectives are hereby established:

1. Set up a promotion system characterized by strict observance of the merit principle;

2. Create equal opportunities for advancement to all qualified and competent employees of the Bureau;

3. Provide a guide for the speedy and fair adjudication of protests of employees against promotion.

II. SCOPE

This Merit Promotion Plan shall cover all positions in the Bureau of Internal Revenue classified under the first and second levels of the career service including those in the regional and/or field offices, except those positions in the Career Executive Service.

III. DEFINITION OF TERMS

1. Promotion - the advancement of an employee from one position to another with an increase in duties and responsibilities as authorized by law and usually accompanied by an increase in salary.

2. Merit Promotion - a systematic method of selecting employees for advancement or promotion on the basis of their qualifications, fitness, and ability to perform the duties and assume the responsibilities of the position being filled.

3. Career Service - a category of service in the Philippine Civil Service characterized by entrance to positions based on merit and fitness to be determined as far as practicable by competitive examinations, opportunity for advancement to higher career positions, and security of tenure.

4. First Level Positions - positions falling under the group of clerical, trades, crafts, and custodial services which involve sub-professional work in a non-supervisory or supervisory capacity requiring less than four (4) years of collegiate studies.

5. Second Level Positions - positions falling under the group of professional, technical, and scientific services requiring completion of four (4) years college studies and appropriate civil service eligibility in a supervisory or non-supervisory capacity up to Division Chief level. cd

6. Qualification Standards - statement of the minimum qualifications for a position which shall include education, experience, training, civil service eligibility, physical characteristics and personality traits required by the position.

7. Next-in-Rank Position - refers to a position which by reason of the hierarchical arrangement of positions in the BIR is in the nearest degree of relationship to a higher position, taking into account the following:

a. organizational structure/s as reflected in the approved organizational chart;

b. salary grade allocation;

c. classification and/or functional relationship of positions; and

d. geographical location.

8. Qualified Next-in-Rank - refer to an employee appointed on a permanent basis to a position previously determined to be next-in-rank to the vacancy proposed to be filled and who meets the requisites for appointment thereto as previously determined by the appointing authority and approved by the Civil Service Commission. aisa dc

9. Promotional Line-up - a listing of incumbents of positions next-in-rank to a vacancy as well as those who, though not next-in-rank, are deemed qualified and competent, together with all necessary information about each incumbent.

10. Superior Qualifications - an outstanding relevant work experience and specialized academic preparation or training appropriate for the position to be filled. It shall include an outstanding performance representing an extraordinary level of achievement and commitment in terms of quality and time, technical knowledge and skill, ingenuity, creativity and initiative, and demonstration of exceptional job mastery in all areas of responsibility.

11. Open Position - refer to those positions that do not have any position next-in-rank which may be filled by lateral/vertical entry.

12. Geographical Location - shall mean the location of the position to be filled and position/s to be considered next-in-rank to the same. If the position to be filled is in the first level, the determination of the next-in-rank positions may be limited in a particular Region/Office/Department/Bureau where the position is.

For second level positions, however, the determination of the next-in-rank positions should be on an agency-wide basis regardless of the location of the position.

13. Functional Relationship - shall mean the correlation between the position to be filled and the position to be considered next-in-rank taking into consideration the duties and responsibilities of both positions.

IV. BASIC POLICIES

1. To be considered for promotion, employees in the Bureau of Internal Revenue must meet the following conditions:

a. Must occupy positions next-in-rank to the vacancy;

b. Must meet the minimum Qualification Standards of the vacant position;

c. Must be included in the Final List of Promotable Employees submitted by the Service Chiefs/Regional Directors.

2. When a position in the First Level becomes vacant, employees in the BIR who occupy the next lower positions in the occupational group under which the vacant position is classified, and in other functionally related occupational groups, who are competent, qualified, and with the appropriate civil service eligibility shall be considered for promotion.

3. When a position in the Second Level becomes vacant, employees in the BIR who occupy the next lower positions in the occupational group under which the vacant position is classified, and in other functionally related occupational groups, who are competent, qualified, and with the appropriate civil service eligibility shall be considered for promotion.

Employees in other government agencies who occupy the next-in-rank positions and who possesses the technical and special qualifications not possessed by BIR employees shall also be considered for promotion to the vacancy.

4. Pursuant to CSC MC #15, s. 1992, employees who are incumbents of next-in-rank positions who meet the qualification requirements for the position to be filled and who are on scholarship grants either here or abroad may be considered for promotion. The performance rating of the employee for the last rating period prior to the scholarship grant shall be used as the basis for the promotion. Such performance rating should at least be Very Satisfactory.

The specific policies of the Bureau such as academic standing as a factor in the consideration for promotion, date of assumption of duty, effectivity of promotion and others, may be subject of a collective negotiation by duly accredited employee association. The Commissioner may create a Committee with a representative of the rank-in-file employees to decide on the matter.

5. All candidates for promotion shall be screened by a Selection Board which shall have the following composition pursuant to CSC MC 18, s. 1988, as amended by CSC MC 38, s. 1989:

a. An official of the Bureau directly responsible for personnel management;

b. A representative of management;

c. A representative of the Service/Office where the vacancy is;

d. Two (2) representatives of the rank and file employees, one from the First Level and one from the Second Level who shall both be chosen at large by the employees through a general election called for the purpose.

6. The comparative degree of competence and qualification of the employees shall be determined by the following criteria:

a. Performance - this shall be based on the latest performance rating of the employee. No employee shall be considered for promotion unless the latest performance rating is Very Satisfactory. cd

The performance rating should be submitted to the Personnel Division thirty (30) days after the end of each semester. If the said rating is not available, candidates for promotion in the Final List of Promotable Employees who do not have the Performance Appraisal Report Form shall not be included in the promotional line-up. cdtai

b. Education and Training - these shall include educational background and the successful completion of training courses, scholarships, training grants and others which must be relevant to the duties and responsibilities of the position to be filled.

c. Experience and Outstanding Accomplishment - these shall include occupational history, work experience and accomplishments. Civil Service awards and other awards for outstanding accomplishments shall be given consideration.

d. Physical Characteristics and Personality Traits - these refer to the physical fitness, attitudes and personality traits of the employees which must have a bearing on the position to be filled.

e. Potential - this is an estimate or prediction of an employee's capacity and ability to perform the duties of the position to be filled and those of higher or more responsible positions in the line of promotion. The prediction shall be based on factors 6.a to 6.d above, i.e. past performance, educational qualifications and/or training, past work experience or occupational history and outstanding accomplishments, physical condition, attitude and aptitude and all other factors that may help in predicting the employee's ability to efficiently perform the duties of the position to which he shall be promoted and of other more responsible positions in the line of promotion.

7. In cases where the qualifications of employees are comparatively equal, preference shall be given to the employee in the organizational unit where the vacant position exists. In cases where all things are still equal, seniority in the position or in the functionally related position shall be considered.

8. A next-in-rank employee who is qualified and competent shall not be promoted if he rejects the new assignment as a result of the promotion because of geographical location. The vacancy may be filled by one who is qualified, competent, and willing to accept the assignment.

9. No other civil service eligibility shall be required for promotion to higher positions in the same level of the career service and within the same functionally related grouping of position.

10. Insiders are given preference for promotion to a hiring level position provided they are competent and qualified as evaluated by the BIR Personnel Selection Board.

11. No outside recommendation for promotion in favor of an employee, whether oral or written, shall be considered. The employee with outside recommendation shall undergo and pass the usual screening process/procedures.

12. Lack of confidence shall not be accepted as a reason for disqualifying an employee from promotion. The reason must be real and substantial.

13. In the event of changes in the organizational structure or occupational grouping, the line of promotion shall be determined on the basis of the new organizational grouping.

14. In filling new positions, except at the lowest level, existing positions in the organization which are similar or allied to the position shall be considered next-in-rank to the new position.

15. An employee who has a pending administrative case shall be disqualified for promotion during the pendency thereof. If found guilty, he shall be disqualified for promotion for a period based on the penalty imposed.

A pending administrative case shall be construed as follows:

a. when the appointing authority has already filed a formal charge; or

b. in case of a complaint of a private person, a prima facie case is already found to exist by the disciplining authority.

16. An appointment though contested shall take effect immediately upon its issuance provided that if the appointee assumes the duties of the position he shall be entitled to receive the salary attached to the position. However, the appointment together with the decision of the BIR Commissioner shall be submitted to the Civil Service Commission for appropriate action within thirty (30) days from the date of its issuance; otherwise, the appointment shall become ineffective thereafter. Likewise, such an appointment shall become ineffective in case the protest is finally resolved in favor of the protestant, in which case the protestee shall be reverted to his former position. cdt

V. PROCEDURES ON PROMOTION

1. The Chief, Personnel Division, shall furnish the Assistant Commissioners (Services) and the Regional Directors copies of the Plantilla of Personnel. In the regional offices, the Chief, Administrative Branch, shall notify in writing the Chief of Branches and Revenue District Officers about the vacancies in the region at the end of each quarter.

2. The Chief, Personnel Division/Chief, Administrative Branch of the regional offices shall post the list of vacancies in three (3) conspicuous places in the office and cause its publication in a daily newspaper with a wide circulation.

3. Pursuant to RMO No. 26-83, at the end of each performance rating period, the Assistant Commissioners, Regional Directors, and Heads of Offices under the Office of the Commissioner shall submit to the Personnel Division a Final List of Promotable Employees. No addendum nor supplemental list shall be allowed. The Final List of Promotable Employees for vacancies falling within the jurisdiction of the Regional Director shall no longer be submitted to the Personnel Division.

4. To effectively implement transparency on promotion, the List of Promotable Employees as prepared in the Revenue Districts, Branches, and divisions shall be posted in a conspicuous place, within their respective offices for the information and guidance of their employees. The Final List of Promotable Employees as decided upon by the Region/Service shall also be posted in a conspicuous place in the Administrative Branch of the Region and the offices of the Assistant Commissioner, respectively.

5. The Chief, Personnel Division/Chief, Administrative Branch, shall make a preliminary evaluation of the qualifications of all candidates for promotion taking into consideration the qualification standards and job requirements of the vacancy. To determine the comparative competence and qualifications of the candidates for promotion, they shall be compared on the basis of the following factors: Performance, Education and Training, Experience and Outstanding Accomplishments, Physical Characteristics and Personality Traits and Potential. 

6. The promotional line-up of employees deemed qualified and competent for promotion to a vacancy shall be prepared. The list shall also contain comparative information of the candidates qualifications and other relevant information. All members of the Selection Board shall be furnished copies of the promotional line-up before a meeting.

7. The Selection Board shall determine the most qualified and competent candidates in the promotional line-up, guided by Section 5, Rule 6 of CSC Resolution No. 83-343 (Rule on Promotion).

The Selection Board shall determine en banc the list of employees recommended for promotion from which the appointing authority may choose the employee to be promoted.

8. The Selection Board shall recommend to the Commissioner, the employee to be promoted based on the Final List of Promotable Employees, while the Regional Selection Board shall recommend to the Regional Director, for positions delegated to him. The recommendation of the Selection Board has great weight.

9. The Personnel Division shall inform the Services/Regional Offices who among those in the Final List of Promotable Employees have been selected by the Board for promotion. This information shall be posted in a conspicuous place in the Personnel Division/Administrative Branch for the information of all the employees concerned.

10. A corresponding appointment shall be prepared by the Chief, Personnel Division/Chief, Administrative Branch for the signature of the Commissioner/Regional Director for submission to the CSC Field Office for attestation.

VI. PROTEST

1. Who may file protest

Only a qualified next-in-rank employee who is not considered for promotion to the next higher position may file a protest with the Commissioner of the Bureau.

2. Form and Content of Protest

The Protest shall be written in clear, simple and concise language, in a systematic manner, and shall have a caption as shown in the attached sample. The aggrieved party shall be called the "Protestant" and the proposed appointee, the "Protestee";

Provided: That where the Commissioner after evaluation finally decides in favor of the protestant, the protestee who decides to file his protest shall be called the "Protestee-Appellant" and the former protestant, the "Protestant-Appellee". cda

The protest shall contain the following:

a. The position contested including its item number and the salary per annum of both the protestant and the protestee;

b. The full name, office, position and salary per annum of both the protestant and the protestee;

c. The specifications of the protest;

d. The comparative qualifications data of both the protestant and protestee showing their education and training, experience, outstanding accomplishments, civil service eligibility, latest performance rating accompanied by a certified true copy of the approved organizational chart/s of the Department/Agency where either or both belong as well as the updated personal data sheets of the protestee and protestant. cd i

3. When to file Protest

The protest may be filed within fifteen (15) days from notice by the protestant of the issuance of the appointment or promotion.

Failure to file a protest within the prescribed period shall be deemed a waiver of one's right and no protest shall thereafter be entertained.

4. Procedure in filing protest

a. The aggrieved party shall file his protest in triplicate directly to the Commissioner and to the Selection Board within the prescribed period.

b. The Selection Board shall within three (3) days from receipt of the protest, refer the same for comment to the recommending authority, which comment shall be filed with the former within five (5) days. In case of failure on the part of the recommending authority to file his comment within the said period, the case shall be decided on the basis of the records at hand.

c. The Selection Board shall decide a protest case within sixty (60) days from receipt of the protest.

d. Either party may, within fifteen (15) days without extension from receipt of the decision, file with the Head of the Department/Agency a motion for reconsideration of the decision, which shall be decided upon within five (5) days from receipt thereof. Only one motion for reconsideration shall be entertained.

5. If the aggrieved party is not satisfied with the decision, he may elevate his protest to the Merit Systems Protection Board (MSPB), Civil Service Commission within fifteen (15) days without extension from receipt thereof.

VII. RESPONSIBILITY

The Chief, Personnel Division, shall be responsible for the preparation/amendment of the Bureau's Merit Promotion Plan subject to the review and approval of the Commissioner of Internal Revenue. He shall also be responsible for the dissemination of the MPP to all concerned employees of BIR. He shall also see to it that the proposals for promotion are in accordance with the provisions of the MPP. aisa dc

VIII. EFFECTIVITY

This Merit Promotion Plan shall take effect upon its approval thereof by the Civil Service Commission. Any subsequent changes in, or amendments to this MPP shall be subject to the approval of the Civil Service Commission and shall take effect six (6) months after its approval. cd

IX. REPEALING CLAUSE

All provisions of existing orders, instructions, and circulars inconsistent herewith are hereby superseded or revoked.

Original Law.Subject: Performance Evaluation System
Original Law.To: All Revenue Officials and Employees

Details.Details:
Pursuant to the provisions of Rule IX of the Omnibus Rules Implementing Book V of Executive Order 292 which took effect on February 14, 1992, the Performance Evaluation System is hereby established. The System shall have the following integral components:

I. OBJECTIVES:

1. To serve as reference in performance planning and review;

2. To serve as objective basis for all personnel actions such as promotion, transfer, reassignment, demotion and separation; and

3. To serve as reference in the grant of performance-based salary step increment as provided for CSC-DBM Joint Circular No. 1, s. 1990; and for other incentives and rewards that may be provided under the approved Employee Suggestions and Incentive Awards System of the agency.

4. To improve the performance of employees in their jobs through a continuing appraisal procedure that considers planning for future action and evaluating past employee performance.

5. To develop the opportunity for self-appraisal so that the employee can evaluate his own performance, determine and devise ways to improve his weaknesses and build on his strengths and hereby become a more viable member of the organization.

6. To promote the most effective use of manpower in the organization in order that the employee makes his/her optimum contribution in the delivery of basic services. cdtai

II. BASIC POLICIES:

1. The Performance Evaluation System shall be made an integral part of the HRD program of this agency.

2. Appraisal shall focus on results/outputs rather than on activities/processes.

3. Employees shall be given appropriate recognition for their performance and contribution to the overall effectiveness and efficiency of the organization.

4. Each supervisor and subordinate shall be informed of his rights and obligations under the Performance Evaluation System and be periodically informed of his progress.

5. Appropriate training opportunities shall be continually provided to facilitate effective implementation of this system.

III. SCOPE:

The System shall apply to all career employees of the Bureau of Internal Revenue.

IV. RATING PERIOD:

Performance evaluation shall be done every six (6) months ending on June 30 and December 31 of every year. However, if there is a need for a shorter or longer rating period, the minimum appraisal period shall be at least ninety (90) days or three (3) months while the maximum appraisal period shall not be longer than one (1) year.

V. PROCEDURE:

The performance evaluation system shall follow the following processes:

1. Discussion of Duties

There shall be a planning session at the start of the rating period during which targets or expected outputs shall be set jointly by the supervisor and subordinates. The supervisor and subordinates define the job of each member of the group, agree on the duties and responsibilities attached to a particular job, and establish the standards on which specific work outputs and behaviors shall be measured.

2. Setting Commitments

Targets/major duties and responsibilities established during the planning session shall be listed in the Performance Evaluation Report Form under the PLANNED column. Agreements shall be jointly signed by both supervisor and subordinates at the start of the rating period. Copies of the Planned Targets shall be furnished the Chief, Personnel Division within thirty (30) days after signing the agreements.

3. Progress Review:

This process involves a discussion between a supervisor and a subordinate using the following steps:

1. Subordinate reviews the progress of all the jobs assigned to him. He shall submit Monthly Accomplishment Report to his supervisor.

2. The supervisor reinforces progress on job goals already accomplished by recognizing employee's efforts and praising him for specific achievements.

3. They both discuss goals and standard not met and identify causes.

4. They identify and agree on appropriate action to overcome causes of difficulties.

5. They re-negotiate goals and standards where necessary.

6. Supervisors shall keep a "Logbook of Critical Incidence" as a tracking device to record the causes of the subordinate's failure in meeting his targets.

4. Discussion of results

There should be a highly interactive performance appraisal discussion and feedback mechanism to foster better working relationship between supervisor and subordinate.

At the end of the evaluation period, the supervisor and subordinate meet to discuss the results of the employee's efforts to meet the targets previously established.

In checking results, the supervisor should do all he can to assist the employee. This assistance may take many forms such as coaching, training, counselling, or reassignments. If the employee still fails to reach his targets after the various means of assistance have been employed, appropriate disciplinary action should be taken against him. On the other hand, the employee who excels in the achievement of his targets should be given recognition. If he cannot be promoted, other forms of rewards should be given.

VI. MECHANICS OF RATING:

A. Appraisal

1. The employee evaluates his own work performance and behavior using the standards set for specific work outputs and behavioral factors affecting performance.

This evaluation shall be based on the information contained in the division logbook, attendance records, accomplishments book and other relevant documents.

2. The supervisor and subordinate meet to discuss and agree on the rating and develop plans for work improvement.

3. The supervisor and subordinate complete the Performance Evaluation Report Form.

4. The duly accomplished forms are submitted to the authorized official for review. If the authorized official agree with the employee's rating, he signs the report form. If not, he should notify the employee and rater and discuss the change in the rating with them. The revised rating shall be initialed by the employee, rater and reviewer.

5. The original copy of the final rating shall be sent to the Personnel Division, copy furnished the employee and the rater.

If the employee disagree with the final rating, he shall also sign the report and/or initial the changes. He may then appeal his rating in accordance with the rules and procedures for the purpose.

B. Rating for Job Accomplishments

The performance Evaluation Report Form shall reflect the results of the appraisal of the performance of an individual employee. Only one (1) form is adopted for rating both supervisory and non-supervisory personnel.

1. To get the Average Point Score, add all the scores assigned under Quantity, Quality and Time by the total number of entries.

2. Multiply the Average Point Score by .7 (70%) to get the Equivalent Point Score.

C. Rating Employee's Behavior

1. The graphic scale presents four (4) behavioral factors for non-supervisors and five (5) for supervisors, affecting the performance of every employee.

2. For each factor there are five (5) levels of performance or anchors which range from Outstanding (10) to Poor (2). Choose the level of performance that gives the most accurate description of the employee's behavior.

3. Add all the corresponding scores and divide the sum by the total number of behavioral factors to get the Average Point Score.

4. Multiply the Average Point Score by .3 (30%) to get the Equivalent Point Score.

D. Overall Rating

The overall rating is computed by adding the Equivalent Point Scores for both Job Accomplishment and Behavior. The sum is the overall rating. Use the indicated rating scale to find the Equivalent Adjectival Rating of the obtained overall rating.

The adjectival ratings are defined as follows:

VII. MECHANISM OF APPEAL:

An employee who expresses dissatisfaction with the rating given him may appeal to the Grievance Committee established under CSC MC No. 45, s. 1989 within fifteen (15) days after receipt of his copy of the Performance Evaluation Report Form . The appeal should specify what his performance rating should be and supporting documents to support his appeal.

VIII. SANCTIONS:

Sanctions against rater who use PES to give undue advantage or disadvantage to people they rate.

IX. EFFECTIVITY:

This Performance Evaluation System will be made effective upon the approval of the Civil Service Commission.

Original Law.Subject: Career and Personnel Development Plan
Original Law.To: All Revenue Officials and Employees

Details.Details:
Pursuant to the provisions of Rule VIII, Book V of Executive Order No. 292, relative to the development and retention of a highly competent and professional workforce in the public service, the Bureau of Internal Revenue formulates this Career and Personnel Development Plan that will provide a continuing program for career and personnel development of its officials and employees. cd i

OBJECTIVES

It is the policy of the Bureau of Internal Revenue to provide all employees with development programs that are necessary in effecting increased productivity and high level of performance. Specifically, the plan aims to:

1. Rationalize all personnel management policies, procedures, and practices of the revenue service.

2. Provide opportunities for personal development and career mobility within the office.

3. Optimize manpower utilization through sound administrative policies and personnel programs which considers both individual competencies and performance requirements.

4. Establish support mechanisms/activities which will foster human resource planning at the organization level and individual career planning at the employee level.

COMPONENTS OF THE PLAN

This Career and Personnel Development Plan contains provisions in all aspects of personnel management and administration. It is the overall human resource development program of the Bureau of Internal Revenue that outlines the principles, procedures, and activities in defining the career and development opportunities available in the revenue service.

I. Recruitment and Selection

Appointment to any career positions in the BIR is made on the basis of merit and fitness. Opportunity for employment is open to all Filipino citizens who possess the appropriate qualifications for the vacant position. In order to attract the best qualified, however, final selection is made on the basis of a comparative assessment of all qualified candidates who have passed the bureau's requirements and screening procedures herein enumerated.

1. Qualification Standards - identify the minimum requirements for a position in terms of education, training and experience, and civil service eligibility. Only those who possess such minimum requirements can be considered for appointment. See Annex "A" for the QS of existing positions in the BIR.

2. Psychological Examination - refers to the standardized written examination which measures personality dimensions, mental ability, and verbal facility of the candidates.

3. Personal Interview - refers to the assessment of individual candidate's skill in oral communication and presentation of ideas.

4. Selection Board - refers to the committee that assess the comparative qualifications of candidates for recruitment and recommends to the Commissioner the best qualified candidate for appointment.

5. Probationary Period - an integral part of the selection process to determine the new appointees suitability or fitness for the position. A person issued an original permanent appointment must serve a probationary period of six (6) months following such original appointment during which he undergoes a thorough character investigation in order to acquire permanent civil service status. A probationer may be dropped from the service for unsatisfactory conduct or want of capacity anytime before the expiration of the probationary period, but such action is appealable to the Civil Service Commission:

II. Merit Promotion

This component of the CPDP provides opportunities for the advancement of incumbent employees from one position to another. Such advancement is characterized by an increase in salary. The Complete promotion procedures in BIR is contained in the Merit Promotion Plan under Annex "B" and Systems of Banking Position under Annex "C".

III. Performance Management

This component provides the venue for facilitating productivity and effectiveness through the review, assessment, and diagnosis of employee performance. cd

1. Evaluation of Individual Performance

All employees in the revenue service will undergo a semestral evaluation of individual performance to determine the extent to which they are contributing to the attainment of the revenue tax goal. Individual performance shall be evaluated based on the comparison of actual against planned outputs. Please see Annex "D" (Performance Evaluation System).

2. Staff Management and Supervision

All employee exercising supervisory functions are responsible for the direct supervision and management of their respective personnel. The mechanisms enumerated below form part of supervisory responsibilities and are considered as measures of supervisory performance effectiveness.

2.a Performance Monitoring

The periodic discussions between supervisor and subordinate to check on the latter's progress relative to his performance targets. The discussions may also focus on problems and constraints that arise in the workplace. As a result of these discussions, appropriate job coaching and problem solving techniques are applied. These activities should be properly reflected in the supervisor's performance report.

2.b Counselling

The periodic discussions between supervisor and subordinate focusing on any issue or problems affecting the subordinate's performance, both personal or work related. The counselling sessions open lines of communications at the lowest level and effect a "worry-free" work environment. The Supervisor's responsibility includes assisting the employee to find and apply appropriate measures to problems/issues raised. Such measures/solutions arrived at during the conduct of counselling sessions should be properly reflected in the supervisor's performance report. acd

2.c Career Planning

The periodic discussions between the supervisor and subordinate where the latter draws up his career goals, aspirations and plans. The supervisor's responsibility includes identifying the career opportunities in the BIR, suggesting or recommending the appropriate development package to be applied to specific employee needs, and monitoring the application of the development package towards the achievement of the employee's career goals. All activities undertaken should be properly reflected in the supervisor's Performance report.

IV. Employee Suggestions and Incentive Award

This component of the CPDP provides for the application and grant of incentives and awards in recognition of individual achievements in the performance of his duties. Attached herewith is the Employee Suggestions and Incentive Award System of the BIR found in Annex "E".

V. This component of the CPDP provides for the creation of a work environment characterized by dynamic and progressive employee-management relations by encouraging the active participation of rank and file employees in matters affecting them. In the BIR, the mechanisms for ensuring staff involvement in management decisions includes the following:

1. Selection Board - refers to the committee in charge of screening and recommending to the appointing authority the candidates for appointment or promotion to any vacant position. The functions and responsibilities, and the composition of the Selection Board is prescribed under the Merit Promotion Plan.

2. Personnel Development Committee - refers to the committee in charge of screening and recommending incumbent personnel to attend training and scholarship programs. The functions and responsibilities of this committee follows the guidelines under CSC Memorandum Circular No. 10, s. 1989.

3.  Incentives and Awards Committee - refers to the committee in charge of screening and recommending the grantees/nominees to any of the incentives and awards program of the bureau. The functions and responsibilities of this committee is prescribed under the Employee Suggestions and Incentives Award System. See Annex "E".

4. Grievance Machinery - refers to the system of resolving any and all complaint or grievance by or aggrieved employee. See Annex "F".

VI. Human Resource Training and Development

This component provides opportunities to maintain or enhance individual work effectiveness, improve underperformance, and prepare employees for higher responsibilities. In the BIR, the development package comes in the form of formal training from the beginning to the end of the employee's stay in the revenue service. Attached as Annex "G" is the training program of the BIR as prepared by the Career Development Division. Another opportunity for human resource development are the scholarship and study availed of by revenue employees thru NEDA and DOF. 

VII. Employee Welfare and Services

This component refers to the medical and dental services and sports and other recreational activities sponsored by BIR top management.

1. Health Services - include the medical and dental services conducted and managed by the Medical and Dental Division under the supervision of the Administrative Service. The staff of this Division, aside from administering the needs of the employees in the National Office, go on regular field visitation to all the regional offices of the BIR.

2. Sports and Other Recreational Activities - include the annual and monthly sports activities and other year round fitness and recreational activities sponsored by BIR top management.

2.a Anniversary Sportfest - refers to the annual report activities participated in by all BIR employees and officials like basketball, volleyball, table tennis, chess, etc.

2.b Chorale Group - refers to the BIR Chorale Society which bagged the championship twice in the DOF inter-agency competition. It is composed of selected BIR officials and employees.

2.c BIR Girl Society - refers to a select of beautiful and talented young ladies of the BIR chosen during the anniversary month of the BIR. These young ladies assist in the tax campaign of the bureau. They also managed the collection and distribution of relief goods to calamity areas of the country.

STRATEGY FOR IMPLEMENTATION

I. Direction Setting

1. The annual work plan which is submitted by all units and offices of the BIR at the end of each year identifies the program objectives, directions and priority targets.

2. Based on the Qualification Standards and position description form, the employee, together with his immediate supervisor, identifies the performance targets for a 6-month period. The accomplished performance target worksheet is submitted to the Personnel Division with thirty (30) from the end of each semester.

3. The employee draws a career plan for himself with the assistance of the immediate supervisor using as basis the system of ranking positions and the available development opportunities. This Career Planning will already identify the development package to help the employee attain his career goal.

4. The Personnel Division reviews/analyzes the pertinent information in the personal data base. The Career Development Division in consultation with immediate supervisors or division chiefs prioritizes the development needs of employees and schedules/recommends them for inclusion or enrolment in any of the available/applicable training and development courses.

II. Performance Review

1. The employee submits his Performance Evaluation Report which will be reviewed and validated by the supervisor. The resulting performance rating of the employee will serve as basis for recommendations for promotion, incentives and awards, and other personnel actions or administrative decisions. cd

2. The Personnel Division consolidates the performance reports and using other informations from the personnel data base, establish a pool of candidates for any of the following opportunities: promotion, training, scholarship, better assignment, incentives, and awards. The performance evaluation report shall be the main basis for inclusion in the list of promotable employees.

3. The employee-management councils (Selection Board, Personnel Development Committee, and SIAC) screen the candidates and recommend the final nominees to the Commissioner of Internal Revenue.

III. Application of Development Packages

1. The Career Development Division shall continuously conduct training and development programs for all employees in response to their individual training/development needs, in cases where the training programs are not available in the BIR, employees can avail of external training programs or scholarships from such agencies like the CSC, NEDA and DOF, on a need basis, and in accordance with the priorities of the bureau.

2. The Personnel Division will continuously update personnel records of employee in order that the list of candidates for development opportunities may likewise be updated.

3. The employee should be reached by the development opportunity that may support his career progression and development needs.

VI. Monitoring and Evaluation

1. The supervisor is initially responsible for monitoring the career and development needs and progress of his staff. Any delays, problems or issues encountered in the attainment of each employee's career goals shall be properly discussed with the Personnel Division and Career Development Division.

2. The Personnel Division is primarily responsible for charting and monitoring the career and development progress of all employees. It also has the responsibility of ensuring that this Career and Development Plan is carried out and implemented.

3. A report on the implementation of the CPDP shall be prepared by the Administrative Service on an annual basis for submission to the CSC.

PROVISIONS FOR SMOOTH IMPLEMENTATION OF THE CPDP

I. Promotional appointments shall be filled up as soon as vacancies occur. The Selection Board shall screen candidates based on the MPP.

II. Supervisory and non-supervisory employees who have not been promoted for a period of three (3) years shall be considered for step increments and such other incentives as may be prescribed by the Suggestion and Incentive Award Committee. cd

III. Based on individual career plans and development needs, all employees shall participate in at least one (1) training and development program every year. The Career Development Division in consultation and coordination with supervisors at various level shall prescribe the schedules and respective programs to which employee will participate.

VI. In observance of Civil Service Law and Rules, the BIR may formulate such other programs, policies, or personnel systems as it may deem necessary in improving the CPDP. In case of revision, these guidelines shall subsequently be updated for the information of all concerned.

In case of deviations/exceptions from these guidelines, the recommendations of the immediate supervisors and the employee management councils concerned (SP, PDC, and SIAC) shall be considered by the Commissioner, whose decision on the matter will be final.

EFFECTIVITY

This Career and Personnel Development Plan shall be made effective upon the approval of the Civil Service Commission. cdtai

Original Law.Subject: Grievance Machinery
Original Law.To: All Revenue Officials and Employees

Details.Details:
Pursuant to Section 35 of P.D. 807, Rule III of Civil Service Rules, as amended by CSC Memorandum Circular No. 45, s. 1989, and Rule XII, Book V of Executive Order No. 292, this Grievance Machinery is hereby established for the guidance of all revenue officials and employees.

RATIONALE

The Bureau of Internal Revenue, in its desire to create an atmosphere conducive to good and harmonious supervisor-subordinate relations and the improvement of employee morale, promulgates these rules and regulations governing expeditious, fair, and equitable adjustment of employee complaints and grievances. cdt

OBJECTIVES

The guidelines are intended to help promote peace, harmony, and productivity through a better employee-management relations. Specifically, these guidelines should help the BIR to:

1. Prevent discontentment and disenchantment between and among employees and officials;

2. Establish an orderly method for handling disputes or reactivate the existing Grievance Committee created under RMO No. 5-90;

3. Settle disputes at the lowest possible level of the organization;

4. Allow the parties to appeal from the results of the grievance negotiation step by step until a final, binding, and executory decision is reached.

DEFINITION OF TERMS

The terms used in the guidelines are operationally defined as follows:

1. Complaint - means an employee's expressed (written or spoken) feelings of dissatisfaction with some aspects of his working conditions, relationships or status which are outside his control.

2. Grievance - refers to a complaint in writing which has, in the first instance and in the employee's opinion, been ignored, overridden or dropped without due consideration.

3. Grievance Procedure - refers to the method of determining and finding the best way to remedy the specific cause or causes of the complaint or grievance.

4. Modes of Settling Disputes

4.1 Conciliation - process whereby a third party (conciliator) brings the parties together, encourages them to discuss their differences and assists them in developing their own proposed solutions.

4.2 Mediation - process whereby a third party (mediator) is more active in assisting the parties reach acceptable solutions to the problems and help the disputing parties develop or come out with an acceptable solution. He can even submit his own proposals for the settlement of disputes. aisa dc

4.3 Arbitration - process whereby a third party (individual arbitrator, aboard of arbitrators or an arbitration court not acting legally) is empowered to make a decision which disposes of the dispute.

SCOPE OF GRIEVANCE MECHANISM

Complaints and grievances may exist between and among individual employees, between employee and supervisor, and between employee and management. Provided however, it shall not apply to cases of dissatisfaction with official actions taken by the management or in disciplinary cases.

Complaints and grievances may refer to any of the following:

1. Non-economic issues

1.1 Policies, practices and procedures which affect employees from recruitment to promotion, detail, transfer, retirement, termination, lay-offs, etc.

1.2 Physical working conditions.

1.3 Interpersonal and interorganizational linkages and relationships.

1.4 Arbitrary exercise of discretion and/or management prerogatives.

2. Policies, practices, and procedures on economic issues such as financial and other terms and conditions of employment as fixed by law.

3. Issues between the management and the CSC registered employee associations (PURE and PAREX)

3.1 Economic issues and other economic packages fixed by law.

3.2 Political issues

a. Recognition and coverage of negotiating unit

b. Association security and check off

c. Violation of provisions and/or policies on self-organization.

3.3 Violation of voluntary agreements reached between the association and management. acd

4. Any and all matters giving rise to employee dissatisfaction

BASIC POLICIES

1. Employees shall have the right to present their complaints and/or grievances to the management and have them settled as expeditiously as possible in the best interest of the employee concerned, the revenue service, and the government as a whole.

2. Complaints and grievances shall not apply to cases of dissatisfaction with official actions taken by the management of the Bureau or in disciplinary cases.

3. An employee without resorting to formal grievance procedures, may discuss informally any problem relating to conditions of employment with supervisors.

4. In presenting a complaint or grievance, the employee shall be assured freedom from coercion, discrimination, or reprisal and of speedy and impartial settlement of such complaint or grievance.

5. Complaints and/or grievance shall be considered not only in relation to its alleged object but also in relation to the personal situation of the complainant.

6. Complaints and/or grievance shall be resolved at the lowest possible level in the bureau.

7. Grievance proceedings shall not be bound by formal legal rules and technicalities.

8. An employee shall have the right to appeal decisions on grievances to competent authorities.

COMPOSITION OF THE GRIEVANCE COMMITTEE

A. National Office

1. Deputy Commissioner for Administrative or his representative to act as Chairman acd

2. Two (2) Assistant Commissioners (Administrative and Inspection Services)

3. The Chief, Personnel Division

4. Two (2) rank and file employees chosen at large

5. An Alternate for higher supervisor and employee in case the complaint concerns any of the members of the Committee.

6. Two (2) association members chosen from among themselves to sit in the Committee only for grievance existing between the management and the recognized association

B. Regional Office

1. Assistant Regional Director to act as Chairman

2. Two (2) higher supervisors (Branch Chief and Revenue District Officer)

3. The Chief, Administrative Branch

4. Two (2) rank and file employees chosen at large

5. An alternate for higher supervisor and employee in case the complaint concerns any of the members of the Committee

6. Two (2) association members chosen from among themselves to sit in the Committee only for grievance existing between the management and the recognized association.

GRIEVANCE PROCEDURES

The procedures for asking redress for complaints and grievances shall be as follows:

A. Oral Discussion

A complainant shall present orally his complaints to his immediate supervisor who shall within three (3) days from the date of presentation inform the employee orally of the decision. cda

B. Grievance in Writing

1. If the employee is not satisfied with the oral decision, he may submit his grievance in writing within five (5) working days from the date of the oral decision of his immediate supervisor to the next higher supervisor. The written complaint shall pass thru the immediate supervisor who shall forward the grievance with his comments within five (5) working days to the next higher supervisor, who shall within five (5) working days from receipt thereof inform the employee in writing, thru the immediate supervisor, of the decision. PROVIDED HOWEVER, that where the object of the complaint is the immediate supervisor, the complainant may bring the grievance to the next higher supervisor who shall take proper action within five (5) working days from receipt of the complaint.

2. If the complainant is not satisfied with the decision of the higher supervisor, he may appeal his grievance to the Grievance Committee within five (5) working days from receipt of the decision, thru the higher supervisor. After making his comments, the higher supervisor shall forward the complaint within five (5) working days to the Grievance Committee, who shall within ten (10) working days from receipt of the complaint, conduct an investigation and hearing. The Grievance Committee shall furnish the complainant with a copy of its decision within five (5) working days after the investigation and hearing, thru the higher supervisor and immediate supervisor.

PROVIDED HOWEVER, that where the object of the complainant is the higher supervisor, the complainant may bring his case directly to the Grievance Committee.

3. If the complainant is not satisfied with the decision of the Grievance Committee, he may elevate his grievance thru the Committee to BIR top management within five (5) working days from receipt of the decision. The top management shall make the decision within ten (10) working days after the receipt of the complaint. PROVIDED HOWEVER, that where the object of the complaint is the top management, the complainant may bring his grievance directly to the Civil Service Commission.

4. If the complainant is not satisfied with the decision of the top management, he may appeal or elevate his grievance to the Civil Service Commission. The CSC shall, if necessary conduct an investigation and hearing and render a decision within fifteen (15) working days from receipt of the grievance.

5. The aggrieved party may file a petition for reconsideration with the CSC if he is not satisfied with its decision, within five (5) working days from receipt of the decision. Such petition shall be resolved within five (5) working days from receipt thereof.

6. The Commission's decision is final, binding, and executory unless appeal from said decision is brought to the proper courts.

7. For a member of a recognized association who would like to present grievances through the body, he must submit his grievance in writing thru the association president or his authorized representative. Any and all subsequent actions of the member-employee, immediate supervisor, higher supervisor, Grievance Committee, Top Management, and Civil Service Commission shall pass thru the association president or his authorized representative. aisa dc

If there is a deadlock, either or both parties may appeal to the Public Sector Labor Management Council (PSLMC) thru the Office for Personal Relations which in turn shall submit to the PSLMC its comments within five (5) working days after receipt of the complaint.

The PSLMC shall render its decision within thirty (30) working days thereafter. The decision of the Council shall be final, binding, and executory unless appeal is brought to the proper courts.

8. The complainant shall fill up the grievance form which shall provide the following information:

a) Name of the Complainant

b) Position title

c) Designation

d) Present Section/Division of Assignment

e) Immediate Supervisor

f) Present Department/Unit of Assignment

g) Higher Supervisor

h) Nature of Grievance

i) Settlement desired

j) Signature of Employee

k) Date of filing from the lowest level in the Bureau

DECISION IMPLEMENTATION

Unless appealed, the decision of the concerned authorities shall take effect immediately and/or upon receipt of the decision of all parties involved. cd

RESPONSIBILITIES

All records involving complaints and grievances shall be kept by the Personnel Division of this Bureau and by the Record Officer of the recognized association.

EFFECTIVITY CLAUSE

The grievance machinery shall be made effective upon approval of the Civil Service Commission.

(Sgd.) VICTOR A. DEOFERIO, JR.
Deputy Commissioner
(Officer-in-Charge)
